source.title: Superposition disentanglement of neural representations reveals hidden alignment
source.authors: André Longon; D. Klindt; Meenakshi Khosla

record.tranche_reason: Tests representation alignment across independently initialized models using soft-matching and linear regression, and tests whether SAE disentanglement changes measured alignment.
record.gate_note: The text reports alignment results for toy models, ImageNet-trained DNNs, and DNN-to-brain prediction. Figures 2–5 and 7–8 are present only as figure references and descriptions, not as numerical data in the supplied text; those values are recorded as figure only. The reported feature-arrangement comparison is also included because it measures correspondence across seeded toy models. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains same-architecture models from different seeds (toy autoencoders, ResNet50, ViT-B/16 on ImageNet). It measures cross-seed alignment with soft-matching, semi-matching and ridge regression on base neurons versus SAE latents. It shows shared features held in different superposition arrangements, which bears on V3. It shows measured alignment depends on the basis, metric and layer, which bears on V6. It reports linear-map scores, which bear on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that different superposition arrangements of the same features deflate mapping-based alignment, and that superposition disentanglement is necessary for these metrics to show true alignment. SAE latents typically raise soft-matching and SAE→Neuron regression scores, while SAE→SAE regression usually falls. They caution that SAEs may construct new representations, that DNN superposition cannot be verified directly, and that the model range is limited.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures alignment using soft-matching, semi-matching, and ridge regression, then compares base activations with SAE latents; it does not reproduce the original sources’ convergence experiments or scale-performance sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment changes with metric (soft-matching versus ridge regression) and layer; ResNet50 has lower soft-matching after SAE processing at the intermediate layer but higher scores at the deep layer. The N=8 toy pair also decreases, which the authors associate with low shared-feature overlap.

fits_no_version.finding: Using SAE latents of DNN activations raises ridge-regression prediction of human higher ventral-stream fMRI: +13.9% for ResNet50 and +3.5% for ViT-B/16 (subject 1). Authors say the other three subjects are consistent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Disentangling superposition in DNN representations increases DNN-to-brain linear predictivity.

record.problems: The text notes limited DNN-to-DNN and DNN-to-brain results, no direct verification of superposition arrangements in DNNs, and possible SAE limitations including feature consistency, absorption, and identifiability. Several numerical results appear only in figures in the supplied text; DNN-to-brain results in the main text are reported for one representative subject, with remaining subjects described as consistent.
record.rows_left_out: No reported alignment result was intentionally omitted. Figure-only rows are retained where the text identifies the relevant condition or describes the overall trend.

untested.parts: No scaling or capability sweep, and no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
Only one pair of seeds per setting. No language models.
No stitching, relative representations or unpaired maps. Absolute regression scores, needed to judge 'little loss', cannot be read from the text.
SAE features are not named or matched as interpretable universal features across models.
No variation of neighbour count, input distribution or out-of-distribution data.
Plateau and shared-data or shared-objective explanations are not tested.

missing.what: Shared-feature overlap between seeds, which grows with N (near all 64 features at N=32). This bears on how many features seeds share.
SAE expansion factor for the DNN SAEs, given only in the figures. Possibly several factors were run, which would be another analysis choice.

record.verdict_notes: Most DNN values are figure-only, so verdicts rest on the text's descriptions of direction. V7 links were removed: incomplete alignment here is attributed to SAE error or superposition, not to plateau or shared causes. Brain rows were moved to fits_no_version. Random-SAE control outcomes are not stated in the text. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test convergence as model scale and capability increase across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption vision-language comparison or scaling of cross-modal alignment.
Tests same-architecture seeded toy models and ImageNet DNNs; does not test different architectures learning shared features, or establish that all shared features/subspaces recur.

Tests ridge-regression mapping after source-side SAE disentanglement and compares SAE-to-SAE mapping; does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired mappings, or mapping with little loss across broad model families.
Does not identify or compare recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.
Compares soft-matching, semi-matching, and ridge regression, and reports layer-dependent results. Does not vary neighbor count or systematically vary input distributions or out-of-distribution data.

Reports incomplete and depth/metric-dependent alignment in the tested settings. Does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, or whether alignment reflects a common model of reality.
